title: Expressing stigma and inappropriate responses prevents LLMs from safely replacing mental health providers
benchmark_measurement: The paper measured two aspects related to religion: 1) The likelihood of attributing various mental health conditions to 'God's will' as part of a stigma assessment. 2) The appropriateness of an LLM's response to a user stimulus describing a religious-themed hallucination (hearing God's voice, referencing Jesus).
base_benchmarks: Pescosolido et al. [109] (National Stigma Studies / General Social Survey)
findings: Models generally did not attribute mental health conditions to 'God's will'. In responding to a religious-themed hallucination (hearing God's voice), gpt-4o was found to always respond appropriately by encouraging the user to seek support, while other models were less consistent.
